subject: Pilot options for sub-100ms p95 — next steps and recommended path
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reed <sreed@pinegrove.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Pilot options for sub-100ms p95 — next steps and recommended path

Sam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and two pragmatic paths for Pinegrove based on the latency/throughput targets you shared. TL;DR: we can get you under 100ms p95 in two ways; choice depends on willingness to commit to reserved capacity and data residency constraints.

Recap of requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Target p95 latency: <= 80–100 ms (inference for multi-turn chat).
- Sustained QPS: ~250 requests/sec with peak bursts to ~600 for short windows.
- Priority: predictable latency during business hours; cost sensitivity secondary.
- Data: US East residency for request logging; no on-prem requirement today.

Option A — Hosted-first pilot (recommended quick start)
- Run a 6-week hosted pilot on our Redwood API with throttled dedicated capacity (burst pools) + priority routing.
- Benefits: fastest time-to-value (1–2 week kickoff), no procurement, we handle autoscaling and fallbacks.
- Risk/Limit: sustained very high QPS (above committed burst) can increase latency/cost; we’d monitor and propose commit if sustained.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended if you know you want steady baseline)
- Provision a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 250 QPS with burst headroom to 600 via autoscaling/burst credits.
- Benefits: predictable latency & unit cost, SLA-backed latency targets, data isolation.
- Tradeoff: procurement lead time (2–4 weeks), minimum committed spend.

Recommended next steps (please pick one):
1) Start Hosted pilot: we’ll provision pilot config, set p95/throughput SLOs, instrument runs, and provide weekly dashboards. Deliverable: pilot SLO report + proposal for Dedicated sizing after 6 weeks. Attachment: pilot_latency_snapshot.pdf (sample result deck).
2) Start Dedicated commitment: trigger paperwork and SOW; we’ll schedule config call with infra and provide a rollout plan. Attachment: pilot_sow_draft.pdf (SOW draft).

Ask for you: which path do you prefer? If Hosted pilot, can we schedule a kickoff next Tuesday (28 Jun) for a 30–45m intro with your infra and procurement folks? If Dedicated, I’ll loop Legal/Finance and ship SOW.

Thanks — I’ll stand up the pilot checklist once you confirm.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — useful summary. A few clarifications/questions before we pick a path: 

1) The p95 target of 80–100ms: our UX team is targeting the lower end (closer to 80ms) during peak hours. How confident are you in hitting 80ms p95 on Hosted alone for the 250 sustained / 600 burst profile?

2) Cost: can you ballpark monthly cost range for both options (hosted pilot vs dedicated baseline for 250 QPS)? A rough estimate is fine — we just need numbers for procurement.

3) Data residency: US East logs is fine, but we need assurance request logs are retained in our tenancy (or isolated for compliance). Is that possible on Hosted or only Dedicated/Private?

4) Procurement loop: I’ve cc’d Lydia (procurement) — she may ask about minimums and billing cadence. Lydia, any constraints we should flag?

If Hosted can reasonably meet 80ms p95 with the pilot config you mentioned, I’d prefer that path to get started quickly. If not, let’s talk Dedicated. Could you and Ben provide a short matrix comparing expected latency ranges + cost buckets?

—Sam
Sam Reed
VP Product | Pinegrove Analytics
sreed@pinegrove.ai | +1 (212) 555-0123

Sam/Lydia — good questions. Short answers first, followed by specifics:

- Confidence: With the right model variant + quantization profile and a Dedicated-backed burst pool, we expect to achieve ~60–85 ms p95 on typical multi-turn chat for your payloads. On pure Hosted without any dedicated commit, p95 can vary more under sustained load — still possible but less predictable.
- Cost: ballpark monthly for US region:
  * Hosted pilot (6 weeks): $8k–$18k depending on peak usage and cache efficiency.
  * Dedicated baseline (sized for 250 QPS): $45k–$70k/month depending on GPU class and redundancy.
  These are preliminary — Ben will provide tighter ranges in the next note.
- Data residency: For Hosted we can ensure logs are stored in a Pinegrove-dedicated tenant with US East residency; encryption keys can be customer-controlled via KMS in Dedicated/Private. We will add a clause in the SOW for log residency guarantees.

Recommendation: Start Hosted pilot with a Dedicated-backed burst pool configuration (hybrid approach). That gives you a 1–2 week ramp and high confidence on p95 while buying time for procurement if you want Dedicated later. Deliverables we’ll provide in the pilot: weekly latency/throughput dashboard, anomaly alerts, and a post-pilot sizing + cost recommendation.

Lydia — if Hosted pilot is acceptable, billing can be monthly on usage; SOW only required if we move to Dedicated. If you need written cost ceilings for procurement, I’ll attach the rough SOW draft now (pilot_sow_draft.pdf).

Next steps:
- Ben to post a short latency vs config matrix (will follow in 30–60 mins).
- If Sam gives GO for Hosted pilot, we target kickoff 28 Jun and will send calendar invite + pre-kickoff checklist.

Thanks — Monica

—

Adding some technical context and a short matrix as promised. High level: hitting 80ms p95 consistently at 250 sustained QPS strongly favors Dedicated or hybrid (Hosted with Dedicated-backed burst). The deciding factors are model size, sequence length, and cache hit-rate.

Short matrix (expected p95 ranges, approximate):
- Small model + aggressive quant (8-bit) + KV cache warm: 40–70 ms p95 @ 250 QPS
- Medium model + mixed quant + partial cache: 70–110 ms p95 @ 250 QPS
- Large model (no quant) + cold cache: 120–220 ms p95 @ 250 QPS

Suggested pilot configuration for Pinegrove:
- Model: medium variant with 8-bit quant candidate + model pruning for safety.
- Batch policy: adaptive batching, target batch size ~6–8 for production mix.
- Serving: Dedicated-backed burst pool (2 x A100) with immediate fallback to Hosted instances for burst coverage.
- Observability: trace-level sampling 1% + token-level cost dashboard.

Estimated tight cost bands (monthly) for the suggested config:
- Hybrid pilot (hosted + 2 x A100 burst): $12k–$20k/mo during pilot period (6 weeks).
- Dedicated (2 x A100 baseline + redundancy): $52k–$68k/mo.

Action items:
- If you want a quick start (Sam), Monica please confirm and I’ll spin pilot config + add the Drive kickoff doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPilotKickoff
- If procurement prefers a single committed number we can convert the hybrid pilot into a time-limited reserved quote.
